trial_court: Additional Civil Judge (Sr. DN), Chitradurga, O.S.No.93/2002
case_name: Pandurangappa S/O Patel Rangappa vs N B Dodda Rangappa S/O Patel Rangappa

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Pandurangappa, S/O Patel Rangappa, and others (A-1(a TO e), A-2 & A-3; SRI.CHITHAPPA, ADVOCATE FOR A-1(a TO e), A-2 & A-3;
parties.respondent_defendant: N.B.Dodda Rangappa, S/O Patel Rangappa, and others (R-1(a TO f); BY SRI. SRUTI CHAGANTI, ADVOCATE FOR R-1(a TO f))

facts_of_case: Suit for declaration, partition and separate possession.

legal_principles.principle: A Hindu male to have more than one wife, it could not be contended that the alleged marriage of Patel Rangappa with Sannamma was void.
legal_principles.held: He submitted that this argument was being advanced on the assumption that the averments made in the plaint were true, though that they were in fact not true.

legal_principles.principle: The legitimacy of the children was on the premise that they were born out of a marriage which was not considered as a marriage in the eye of law.
legal_principles.held: He submitted that since prior to 1955, a Hindu male could have multiple wives, the children born through such multiple wives would have to be considered legitimate.

legal_principles.principle: The children born to them would be entitled to succeed to the properties in equal shares.
legal_principles.held: He submitted that as a consequence, since both marriages were valid, the children born to them would be entitled to succeed to the properties in equal shares.

legal_principles.principle: The legitimacy of the children was only on the basis that the marriage between a man and woman was void or voidable.
legal_principles.held: He submitted that the legitimacy of the children was only on the premise that they were born out of a marriage which was not considered as a marriage in the eye of law.

use_for_drafting: advising on Hindu Marriage Act implications
representing family members in inheritance disputes
